content: This information does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common Brand Name(s): Reyataz Uses: This formulation of atazanavir is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection in infants and children. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in the body, allowing the child’s immune system to function more effectively. Atazanavir belongs to a class of drugs known as protease inhibitors. This specific form of atazanavir must be administered with another protease inhibitor, ritonavir, to enhance (boost) the levels of atazanavir in the body. It is important to note that atazanavir is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to others, your child must continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Personal items that may come into contact with blood or other body fluids (e.g., needles, syringes, toothbrushes) should not be shared. How to Use: Before starting atazanavir, read the Patient Information Leaflet and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist. This medication is taken orally. Administer the medication to your child as directed by the doctor, typically once daily. Open the packet and mix its contents with food (e.g., applesauce, yogurt) as instructed. If your child cannot eat solid food, the medication may be mixed with a liquid (e.g., milk, infant formula, or water). For children under 6 months who cannot eat solid food or drink from a cup, mix the medication with infant formula as directed and administer it using an oral syringe. Do not use a baby bottle. Administer the dose within one hour of mixing it with food or liquid. The dosage is determined based on your child’s medical condition, weight, response to treatment, and any other medications they may be taking. For optimal effectiveness, administer this medication at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to continue giving this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by the doctor. Do not skip doses, and do not give more or less of the medication than prescribed. Do not stop administering it (or other HIV medications) without the doctor’s approval, even for a short period. Side Effects: Headache or nausea may occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because the doctor has determined that the benefits to your child outweigh the risks of side effects. As the immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat previously existing infections, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. Additionally, symptoms may arise if the immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while your child is taking this medication (e.g., increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas, decreased fat in the arms and legs). The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Atazanavir commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. However, it may be difficult to distinguish this rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before administering atazanavir, inform the doctor or pharmacist if your child is allergic to it or has any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Atazanavir may increase cholesterol and fat (triglyceride) levels in the blood. HIV infection itself can also contribute to this effect. Elevated cholesterol and triglycerides may increase your child’s risk of heart problems, such as a heart attack. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with the doctor, as well as strategies to reduce the risk of heart disease. This medication may contain aspartame. This form of atazanavir is not typically used by adults and is unlikely to be used during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products your child uses (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with the doctor and pharmacist. Atazanavir can slow the removal of other medications from your child’s body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Similarly, other medications can influence the removal of atazanavir from the body, which may impact its effectiveness. Examples include apalutamide, bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, lumacaftor, certain rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifapentine), and certain seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone). Prescription and nonprescription drugs used to treat heartburn, indigestion, or ulcers (e.g., H2 blockers like famotidine, proton pump inhibitors like lansoprazole/omeprazole) reduce stomach acid and may decrease the absorption of atazanavir. This could prevent atazanavir from working effectively. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., viral load, T-cell counts, kidney/liver function, cholesterol/triglyceride levels, blood sugar levels) should be conducted while your child is taking this medication. Ensure all medical and lab appointments are kept. Missed Dose: If a dose is missed, administer it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and administer the next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not open the packet until ready to use. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
